feature: Implement dynamic imports for Monaco Editor with code splitting
workflow_rationale: This is a single-service frontend optimization task focused on improving bundle size and initial page load. No multi-service coordination or complex migration needed - just targeted webpack and import optimizations.

phases.name: Audit Current Monaco Imports
phases.description: Analyze all Monaco Editor imports to identify optimization opportunities and measure baseline bundle size

subtasks.description: Search for all Monaco imports and verify no top-level imports exist

verification.expected: Should document all non-type Monaco imports

subtasks.description: Analyze current bundle size with webpack-bundle-analyzer

verification.command: npm run build && npm run analyze
verification.expected: Bundle analyzer runs successfully and generates report

subtasks.notes: Successfully configured webpack-bundle-analyzer. Added package to devDependencies, created 'analyze' script, and integrated BundleAnalyzerPlugin into next.config.mjs. Verified by running analyze script - reports generated at .next/analyze/client.html (1.4M) and .next/analyze/server.html (293K). Bundle analyzer now provides detailed visualization of bundle composition for optimization analysis.

subtasks.description: Document baseline metrics: initial bundle size, Monaco chunk sizes, and load time

verification.instructions: Review baseline-metrics.json for documented bundle sizes

subtasks.notes: Successfully documented comprehensive baseline metrics including: total bundle size (11M/6M chunks), 344 JS files, main page (27K, no Monaco), editor page (70K + 24K Monaco wrappers). Confirmed Monaco already uses dynamic imports with SSR disabled. Identified optimization opportunities: worker splitting (~1-2MB), language pack splitting, and route preloading. Metrics saved to baseline-metrics.json for post-optimization comparison.

phases.name: Optimize Monaco Worker Loading
phases.description: Configure Monaco to lazy-load language workers and syntax highlighters only when needed

subtasks.description: Create MonacoEnvironment configuration to lazy-load workers
subtasks.notes: Successfully created monaco-worker-config.ts with MonacoEnvironment configuration. Implemented configureMonacoWorkers() function that lazy-loads Monaco Editor workers (JSON, CSS, HTML, TypeScript, editor) using dynamic imports. Workers are loaded on-demand via getWorker() to reduce initial bundle size. Includes debug logging, performance tracking, and helper functions for configuration management. Verification passed.

subtasks.description: Update next.config.mjs to split Monaco workers into separate chunks
subtasks.notes: Added Monaco workers cache group to webpack configuration with priority 35. Workers are now split into separate chunks for optimal lazy loading.

subtasks.description: Integrate worker config into Monaco components
subtasks.notes: Successfully integrated configureMonacoWorkers() into all three Monaco components (AgentMonacoEditor.tsx, monaco.tsx, VisualDiff.tsx). Workers are now configured to lazy-load on demand before Monaco initializes, reducing initial bundle size. Build verified successfully with no new errors.

phases.name: Implement Route-Level Code Splitting
phases.description: Ensure Monaco Editor is only loaded on routes that actually use it, not on the main landing page

subtasks.description: Verify main page (/) doesn't import Monaco components

verification.expected: OK (no Monaco imports on main page)

subtasks.notes: Verification passed - main page (src/app/page.tsx) does not import Monaco or AgentMonacoEditor components. The page correctly uses dynamic imports for PromptInterface and has no direct Monaco dependencies in the initial bundle.

subtasks.description: Ensure editor pages use dynamic imports at route level

checks: Main page loads without Monaco chunk
No monaco files in network tab

subtasks.notes: Successfully implemented dynamic imports for editor pages. Converted AgentMonacoEditor import in src/app/editor/page.tsx and CodeiumPlayground import in src/app/tools/codeium/page.tsx to use Next.js dynamic() with SSR enabled and loading states. Both pages now use route-level code splitting following the pattern from main dashboard, ensuring Monaco bundles only load on editor routes.

subtasks.description: Add preload hints for Monaco on editor routes
subtasks.notes: Added useEffect hook to dynamically inject modulepreload link tags for Monaco Editor and AgentMonacoEditor chunks. Preload hints are added to document head when component mounts and cleaned up on unmount. This improves initial load performance for the editor page by allowing the browser to fetch Monaco resources earlier in the page lifecycle.

phases.name: Enhanced Webpack Code Splitting
phases.description: Configure webpack to create optimal Monaco chunks with minimal duplication

subtasks.description: Split Monaco language packs into separate chunks by language

verification.command: npm run build && ls .next/static/chunks/ | grep -q monaco && echo 'OK' || echo 'FAIL'

subtasks.notes: Successfully split Monaco language packs into separate chunks. Added webpack cache groups for TypeScript (6.4MB), JSON, CSS, HTML, and basic languages. Each language pack now loads lazily on demand. Build verified - Monaco chunks created in .next/static/chunks/. Priorities configured: workers (35) > language packs (34-31) > core editor (30).

subtasks.description: Configure tree-shaking to exclude unused Monaco features
subtasks.notes: Successfully configured tree-shaking for Monaco Editor. Added optimization.usedExports=true and optimization.sideEffects=true to webpack config for client bundles. These settings enable webpack to analyze module exports and eliminate unused code from Monaco Editor and other dependencies. Build verified successfully with no errors - tree-shaking now active for optimal bundle size reduction.

subtasks.description: Add bundle size limits for Monaco chunks

verification.expected: Build warns if Monaco chunks exceed size limits

subtasks.notes: Added bundle size limits for Monaco chunks in next.config.mjs. Build now warns when Monaco chunks exceed 500KB limit. Verified that warnings appear for monaco-language-typescript (6.36 MiB) and monaco-editor (1.49 MiB) chunks.

phases.name: Performance Verification
phases.description: Measure improvements in bundle size and page load performance

subtasks.description: Generate updated bundle analysis and compare with baseline

verification.command: npm run build && npm run analyze
verification.expected: Bundle analyzer shows Monaco chunks are smaller and lazy-loaded

subtasks.notes: Successfully generated final bundle analysis and comparison. Editor page reduced by 64.3% (70K → 25K). Monaco split into core (1.5M) + TypeScript language (6.4M) lazy-loaded chunks. Main page unchanged at 27K with no Monaco. Build verified, bundle analyzer reports generated at .next/analyze/client.html and .next/analyze/server.html. Comprehensive metrics comparison documented in final-metrics.json.

subtasks.description: Test main page load without Monaco overhead
Test editor page Monaco lazy loading
Run Lighthouse performance audit and document improvements

parallel_groups.reason: Both depend only on phase-1-audit and work on different aspects (workers vs routes)

parallelism.speedup_estimate: 1.3x faster than sequential (phases 2 and 3 can run in parallel)

acceptance_criteria: Main page (/) does not load Monaco Editor chunks
Monaco chunks are lazy-loaded only on editor routes
Initial bundle size reduced by at least 2MB
All Monaco features continue to work correctly
No performance regressions on editor pages
